Photograph: Telemundo Kansas City via AP View image in fullscreen Adan Manzano, a Telemundo reporter, was in New Orleans to cover the Super Bowl. Photograph: Telemundo Kansas City via AP Louisiana Two people sentenced to 60 and 45 years in prison in death of Telemundo reporter Danette Colbert and Rickey White sentenced in Adan Manzano’s death for racketeering and negligent homicide Maya Yang Mon 28 Sep 2026 16.10 EDT Last modified on Mon 28 Sep 2026 16.13 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A Louisiana judge has handed lengthy prison sentences to two people convicted of roles in a criminal enterprise that targeted New Orleans tourists led to the death of a reporter covering the 2025 Super Bowl there. Nancy Miller, a state court judge, on Monday sentenced Danette Colbert, 49, to a total of 60 years in prison: fifty years for racketeering and a consecutive 10 years for negligent homicide in the death of Adan Manzano, a journalist for the Spanish-language news outlet Telemundo Kansas City. Colbert’s accomplice, Rickey White, was sentenced to 45 years’ imprisonment for racketeering. The sentences come just days after a jury in the suburban New Orleans community of Jefferson parish, Louisiana, convicted both Colbert and White, 35, for their roles in the 5 February 2025 death of Manzano, 27. Manzano had traveled to the New Orleans area to cover the Kansas City Chiefs’ Super Bowl clash with the Philadelphia Eagles. He was found dead in his hotel room in Kenner, Louisiana, the suburb where New Orleans’ international airport is, days before the Chiefs lost the big game to the Eagles. The Jefferson parish coroner’s office, whose jurisdiction includes Kenner, said Manzano died from positional asphyxiation. An autopsy found Xanax and alcohol in his system. Prosecutors said Manzano was among the victims of a yearslong operation in which Colbert, White and a co-defendant who testified against them – Christian Anderson – targeted unsuspecting tourists in the city’s French Quarter. The group allegedly lured victims with the promise of sex before drugging and robbing them. Prosecutors said the criminal enterprise dated back to 2012. Manzano’s father addressed his son’s death at Monday’s sentencing via a videoconferencing platform. According to a statement from Jefferson parish district attorney Paul Connick’s office, Manzano’s father called the sentencing “a say day for me and my family”. “May the laws of this country lock up the people that destroyed my life,” he testified. “I respectfully ask that you give them the sentencing they deserve.” According to local news channel WVUE , the father added: “They snatched his dreams, life and family as we were seeing him happy and successful.” Manzano’s mother, meanwhile, said: “I don’t want to say anything to the people that committed this crime, because they are beings of darkness, beings that don’t have God in their lives. “But I don’t think they should go on with life causing harm and killing people – because I still can’t accept that Adan is not here … This loss, I’ll never overcome it. I don’t wish this on anybody, on any family.” A cousin of Manzano, Carlos Castillo, reportedly said: “I want to look you guys in the face and say that you should pay your entire life for this … Every time the cell opens and you cannot see the light, you think of my cousin.” Manzano’s wife, Ashleigh Boyd, was killed in an April 2024 car crash in Topeka, Kansas. A Topeka judge found Todd W Armstrong guilty of vehicular homicide, speeding and driving on the wrong side of the road after a one-day trial on 21 September, four days after the jury verdict in Manzano’s death in Louisiana . Boyd and Manzano’s daughter – Eleanor, now three – is being raised by her maternal grandparents. Months after Manzano’s death, Colbert received a 25-year prison sentence for being found to have violated her probation on a prior theft and fraud conviction and being classified a habitual offender. Miller on Monday told Colbert that her “behavior in this matter [is] quite alarming”, according to WVUE. “You were indifferent to the impact that your actions had,” Miller said. “That is evident by your consistent pattern in your criminal history. Apparently, you’ve been doing this for quite some time. It’s finally caught up to you with the death of one of your victims.” Explore more on these topics Louisiana US crime New Orleans news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed US news US politics Midterms 2026 World Climate crisis Middle East Ukraine US immigration Soccer Business Environment Tech Science Newsletters The Filter Wellness

A wildlife overpass for elk, deer, and pronghorn on Interstate 25 between Denver and Colorado Springs. Photograph: UCG/Universal Images Group/Getty Images View image in fullscreen A wildlife overpass for elk, deer, and pronghorn on Interstate 25 between Denver and Colorado Springs. Photograph: UCG/Universal Images Group/Getty Images Colorado Colorado wildlife overpass cut vehicle-animal collisions by 91%, report finds Elk, bear, frogs and other animals have used the overpass, which connects 39,000 acres of habitat, since its completion Dara Kerr Mon 19 Oct 2026 19.17 EDT First published on Mon 19 Oct 2026 17.39 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Colorado officials have tracked herds of elk, bears, pronghorn and even northern leopard frogs ambling across its new wildlife overpass. According to a newly released report, the overpass, which acts as a bridge over a busy stretch of interstate, has helped cut wildlife-vehicle collisions by 91% since its completion 10 months ago. The overpass is the centerpiece of a larger system built by the state to assist wildlife crossing the highway, which also includes miles of 8-ft tall fencing and five large wildlife underpasses. “One of the most heartwarming moments for me was when [Colorado department of transportation] sent me a picture of an elk mama taking her calf under [Interstate-25],” Brandon Marette, a wildlife biologist for Colorado parks and wildlife, told CBS News . “All came to fruition in that one moment. That elk with her calf was just standing there in safety.” The Colorado department of transportation said before the overpass system was built, there was an average of one wildlife-vehicle crash a day in this corridor. Such wildlife crossings are popping up across the country as a way to protect wildlife habitat and reduce collisions, which can result in injuries and deaths in humans and animals. Research has shown that overpass systems are successful in “nearly eliminating” these accidents and that such infrastructure buildouts often “pay for themselves” by preventing costly crashes. Tents, night-vision goggles and bear tracking kits: America’s first nature library opens Read more Nearly 20 wildlife crossings are under way in the US, with the structure in Colorado currently the biggest. The overpass, which sits between the state’s two biggest cities, Denver and Colorado Springs, spans six lanes of traffic and connects 39,000 acres of habitat on both sides of the interstate. The bridge is covered in grass and measures 200ft wide and 209ft long with gradually sloped entrances to ease crossings for animals. This region of Colorado is known for high movement of large game. State officials say that wildlife underpasses and tunnels often don’t work for big animals, such as bull elk, because they restrict mobility and don’t accommodate their antlers. “Elk and pronghorn like these big open structures where they can see for miles in each direction,” Chuck Attardo, the environmental manager for Colorado department of transportation, told CBS News. “For decades, pronghorn going from Trinidad to Greenland were looking for a place to cross on I-25. And when we open this up, we have pronghorn on video using the overpass, and for the first time in decades they’re coming over here to the west side.” While large game animals have been taking advantage of the crossing, officials have also tracked smaller wildlife using the corridor, including mule deer, coyotes, rabbits, frogs and the threatened Preble’s meadow jumping mouse. The project received $22m in federal funding and $8m from the state, but officials say they were able to complete it for just $15m. Now, the Colorado department of transportation says it is hoping to build other wildlife crossings across the state. https://www.digi24.ro/stiri/externe/ue/p.text: NATO nu va organiza un summit în Albania anul viitor, în ciuda planurilor anterioare în acest sens, a declarat joi prim-ministrul albanez Edi Rama, relatează Reuters . Agenția Reuters a relatat în luna iunie că planurile privind organizarea unui summit al Alianței în Albania anul viitor au fost puse sub semnul întrebării din cauza opoziției administrației Trump și a nemulțumirii membrilor NATO față de cheltuielile reduse ale Tiranei în domeniul apărării. În cadrul unui discurs ținut la Dublin înaintea unei reuniuni a liderilor europeni, Rama a declarat: „Problema este că nu există încă o poziție comună cu privire la data la care va avea loc summitul; cu siguranță nu va fi în 2027”. El a adăugat: „Iar în 2028, dacă va avea loc un summit, acesta se va desfășura la Tirana”. NATO ia în considerare renunțarea la practica recentă de a organiza summituri anuale, o măsură care ar putea evita o întâlnire potențial tensionată cu președintele SUA, Donald Trump, spre sfârșitul mandatului acestuia. Cu toate acestea, diplomații afirmă că Alianța ar putea totuși să decidă să organizeze un summit în termen scurt în 2026 — dar nu la Tirana. Un oficial al Alianței a declarat joi că „următorul summit al NATO va avea loc în Albania. Decizia privind data nu a fost încă luată”. Într-o declarație adoptată cu ocazia summitului NATO din iunie 2025 de la Haga, liderii alianței au afirmat: „Așteptăm cu interes următoarea noastră întâlnire din Turcia, din 2026, urmată de o întâlnire în Albania”. Însă, într-o declarație adoptată la summitul alianței de la Ankara, din luna iulie a acestui an, liderii au afirmat: „Așteptăm cu nerăbdare următoarea noastră întâlnire”, fără a preciza data sau locul unui viitor summit. Premierul portughez spune că secretarul general al NATO este „complet deconectat de la realitate”. Declarația care l-a indignat „Nu este nevoie să reinventăm roata”.
